text: Refactoring is a crucial practice in software development. It involves improving the internal structure of code without changing its external behavior. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to understand. For example, you might break a long, complex function into smaller, more focused parts, or rename variables so their purpose is instantly clear. This process directly reduces "technical debt," which is the hidden cost of writing messy code quickly. By regularly refactoring, developers pay back this debt, preventing future problems. Ultimately, good refactoring makes the codebase more readable and maintainable, saving time and effort for the whole team in the long run.
